Subject: Results from initial bakeoff — gap vs. VastAI

Priyom,

Quick update from our side after the POC last week. We ran your recommended config against VastAI's managed endpoint across our standard dataset (attached spec). The early results look promising for Redwood on quality, but we're seeing a ~22% token-cost delta in favor of VastAI and occasional 95th%-tile spikes that worry our infra team.

Procurement is already asking for hard cost comparisons and timeline for a production pilot. Also copying procurement so they can flag where the final supplier decision will hinge (latency consistency and TCO run-rate).

Can your team share a concrete pilot proposal and a short ops runbook we can present to the SRE and procurement reviewers? We need something by EOW to keep the decision window open.

Thanks,
Alex Garner
Director of Product
MarketPulse

Subject: Re: Results from initial bakeoff — gap vs. VastAI

Alex — thanks for the frank note and for sharing the spec. Important context. We read the logs you sent and ran an internal replay overnight. High level: quality parity looks intact; cost gap is primarily driven by their higher batching window plus a different KV-cache warmup. The 95th%-tile spikes correlate with bursty traffic in one of your segments (session rehydration).

Proposal (short):
- 10-business-day perf-validation sprint using a production-like slice of your traffic (we'll use your CSV).
- Dedicated pilot nodes (2x reserved GPUs) with tuned batching and prefix cache enabled for the sprint.
- Ops deliverables: runbook, auto-remediation playbook for cold-cache scenarios, and a snapshot latency report after days 2/5/10.
- Commercial: 6-week trial (no commit) + a one-time credit covering the first 50M tokens of pilot traffic. If pilot meets the SLOs we agree, we convert to a Reserved Capacity term with a 10% first-year discount.

I'm happy to host a 30m alignment call tomorrow to confirm SLOs and the dataset slice. Marissa will own the ops runbook; Karthik will own the bench config. If that sounds good I'll draft the SOW and DocuSign link.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Alex — technical plan from our side (concise):
- We'll run a replay with two model variants: rwl-7b-q4hf (default) and rwl-7b-q4bf (aggressive quant). The latter usually reduces token cost ~12–18% with <1% QoE delta if your prompts fit the tested prefix patterns.
- Batching: we'll align the batching window with your latency SLOs; increasing the batching window by 15–20ms yields ~8% cost improvement without affecting 95th significantly in our sims.
- KV-cache priming: we'll prewarm session caches for repeat-users via a small synthetic preflight. This typically removes the spike pattern you saw.

Operational note: the test will need a short (5–10 minute) maintenance window to seed caches when switching configs. We'll coordinate to minimize customer impact.

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
